Mumbai recorded a maximum temperature of 34.7 degrees Celsius on Friday, while Dahanu reported the highest maximum temperature in Maharashtra at 35.7 degrees Celsius, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
The weather across several parts of Maharashtra remained largely dry, with no rainfall recorded at most reporting stations. The IMD's daily weather bulletin stated that Pune is likely to witness mainly clear skies, becoming partly cloudy towards the afternoon or evening on Saturday. Light rain or thundershowers are expected in the Ghat areas of Pune.
Mumbai records warm day
Mumbai recorded a maximum temperature of 34.7 degrees Celsius, which was 0.4 degrees above normal.
The minimum temperature stood at 27.2 degrees Celsius, 2.9 degrees above normal. At Santacruz, the maximum temperature was 32.6 degrees Celsius, 2.1 degrees below normal, while the minimum was 25.2 degrees Celsius, 2.9 degrees above normal.
Alibag recorded a maximum temperature of 34.5 degrees Celsius and a minimum of 27.4 degrees Celsius. Dahanu reported 35.7 degrees Celsius, the highest maximum temperature in the state, while its minimum temperature was 22.7 degrees Celsius. Ratnagiri recorded a maximum of 33 degrees Celsius and a minimum of 23.9 degrees Celsius.
No rainfall was recorded at the reporting stations across the Konkan region, including Mumbai, Santacruz, Alibag, Ratnagiri and Dahanu.
Pune records 33.5 degrees Celsius
Pune recorded a maximum temperature of 33.5 degrees Celsius, two degrees above normal, while the minimum temperature was 21.9 degrees Celsius, six degrees above normal. At Lohegaon, the maximum temperature was 34.8 degrees Celsius, 3.3 degrees above normal, and the minimum stood at 23 degrees Celsius, 7.1 degrees above normal.
Solapur recorded the highest maximum temperature in Madhya Maharashtra at 35.4 degrees Celsius, followed by Satara at 34.2 degrees Celsius. Sangli recorded 33.6 degrees Celsius, Ahilyanagar 33 degrees Celsius, Kolhapur 32.2 degrees Celsius and Nashik 32.5 degrees Celsius.
Mahabaleshwar recorded the lowest minimum temperature in the state at 17.2 degrees Celsius, while its maximum temperature stood at 25.1 degrees Celsius.
Marathwada sees above-normal temperatures
In Marathwada, Dharashiv recorded a maximum temperature of 33.9 degrees Celsius and a minimum of 18.8 degrees Celsius. Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar recorded 33.6 degrees Celsius as its maximum and 21.2 degrees Celsius as its minimum.
Parbhani reported a maximum temperature of 34.6 degrees Celsius, 2.7 degrees above normal, while its minimum stood at 20.2 degrees Celsius.
Vidarbha records relatively lower maximum temperatures
Several parts of Vidarbha recorded maximum temperatures below 32 degrees Celsius. Akola recorded 31.9 degrees Celsius, Amravati 31.4 degrees Celsius, Chandrapur 31.4 degrees Celsius, Wardha 30 degrees Celsius and Yavatmal 30 degrees Celsius.
Buldhana, Bramhapuri and Nagpur each recorded a maximum temperature of 29.6 degrees Celsius. Gondia reported 26.6 degrees Celsius, the lowest maximum temperature among the listed stations in the region. Yavatmal recorded a minimum temperature of 17.6 degrees Celsius, while Gondia reported 18.5 degrees Celsius.
Pune rainfall remains below normal
Pune recorded 0.3 mm of rainfall in the 24-hour period ending at 8.30 am on Friday. The city's seasonal rainfall stood at 1.7 mm against a normal of 76.5 mm, marking a deficit of 74.8 mm.
For Saturday, the IMD has forecast mainly clear skies in Pune, becoming partly cloudy towards the afternoon or evening. Light rain or thundershowers are likely in the Ghat areas. The maximum and minimum temperatures are expected to be around 34 degrees Celsius and 20 degrees Celsius, respectively.
